summary: Resting at Jacob’s well, Jesus asks a Samaritan woman for a drink, offers her living water, reveals Himself as the Messiah, and many in her town believe.
key_insight: Jesus’ plainest word yet about who He is, “I who speak to you am He,” was spoken not to a teacher in Jerusalem but to a Samaritan woman at a well. And Samaritans are the first in John to call Him “the Savior of the world.”
story: When Jesus knew that the Pharisees had heard He was making more disciples than John, He left Judea for Galilee, and He needed to go through Samaria. He came to Sychar, near the field Jacob had given to his son Joseph. Tired from the journey, He sat down by Jacob’s well. It was about the sixth hour, and His disciples had gone into the town to buy food.

A woman of Samaria came to draw water, and Jesus said to her, “Give Me a drink.” She was startled: “How is it that You, being a Jew, ask a drink from me, a Samaritan woman?” For Jews have no dealings with Samaritans. Jesus answered, “If you knew the gift of God, and who it is who says to you, ‘Give Me a drink,’ you would have asked Him, and He would have given you living water.”

She pointed out that He had nothing to draw with, and the well was deep. “Are You greater than our father Jacob, who gave us the well?” Jesus said, “Whoever drinks of this water will thirst again, but whoever drinks of the water that I shall give him will never thirst.” It would become in him “a fountain of water springing up into everlasting life.” “Sir, give me this water,” she said, “that I may not thirst, nor come here to draw.”

Jesus said, “Go, call your husband, and come here.” “I have no husband,” she answered. Jesus told her she had spoken the truth: she had had five husbands, and the man she now had was not her husband. “Sir,” she said, “I perceive that You are a prophet.” Then she raised the old question between their peoples. Her fathers had worshiped on this mountain, but the Jews said Jerusalem was the place.

“Woman, believe Me,” Jesus said, “the hour is coming when you will neither on this mountain, nor in Jerusalem, worship the Father.” Salvation is of the Jews, He told her, “But the hour is coming, and now is, when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth; for the Father is seeking such to worship Him.” She said, “I know that Messiah is coming,” and, “When He comes, He will tell us all things.” Jesus said to her, “I who speak to you am He.”

Just then His disciples returned. They marveled that He was talking with a woman, yet no one asked Him why. The woman left her waterpot, went into the town and said to the men, “Come, see a Man who told me all things that I ever did. Could this be the Christ?” And the people went out to Him.

Meanwhile the disciples urged Him, “Rabbi, eat.” He said, “My food is to do the will of Him who sent Me, and to finish His work.” He told them to lift up their eyes and look at the fields, “for they are already white for harvest!”

Many Samaritans from that town believed in Him because of the woman’s word. They urged Him to stay, and He stayed two days. Many more believed because of His own word, and they told the woman, “Now we believe, not because of what you said, for we ourselves have heard Him and we know that this is indeed the Christ, the Savior of the world.”

scene.label: Samaritans
scene.text: When Assyria conquered the northern kingdom of Israel, it settled foreign peoples in its cities (2 Kings 17:24). Their descendants mixed with the Israelites who remained. Jews regarded the Samaritans as mixed in blood and in worship, and the hostility ran both ways for centuries.

scene.label: “This mountain”
scene.text: Mount Gerizim rises above Jacob’s well. The Samaritans had built a temple on it, which the Jewish ruler John Hyrcanus destroyed in the late second century BC. They went on worshiping on the mountain, and they accepted only the five books of Moses as Scripture.

scene.label: Jacob’s well
scene.text: Jacob bought land near Shechem (Genesis 33:18–19), and Joseph’s bones were buried there (Joshua 24:32). The Old Testament does not mention the well, but the well near ancient Shechem is still shown today, one of the few Gospel sites whose location is not seriously disputed. It is deep, as the woman said.

scene.label: Living water
scene.text: In everyday speech, living water meant fresh, flowing water from a spring, far better than water standing in a cistern. The prophets used the picture for God Himself: “the fountain of living waters” (Jeremiah 2:13).

scene.label: A coming Prophet
scene.text: Because they held only the books of Moses, the Samaritans probably looked for a coming Prophet like Moses (Deuteronomy 18:15–18). That may be why the woman expects the Messiah to tell them all things.

witnesses.john: John alone tells this meeting, and he places it right after Nicodemus: a respected teacher of Israel who came by night, then an unnamed Samaritan woman at a well. The conversation moves from a request for water to faith in “the Savior of the world,” and it shows the Son giving life beyond the borders of Israel, to the world God loved (John 3:16).

seeing.reveals: Jesus is tired and thirsty, truly human, and at the same time the Giver of living water who knows her whole life and says plainly, “I who speak to you am He.” He crosses the lines that kept Jews from Samaritans to reach one woman and, through her, a town.
seeing.living: Jesus did not pass over her past; He named it, and He kept offering her living water. Being fully known by Him is where hope begins, not where it ends. And like her, you can bring others with a simple invitation: “Come, see.”
seeing.ponder: What are you still drinking from that leaves you thirsty again, and what would it mean to ask Jesus for living water today?

preaching.big_idea: Jesus knows everything you have done and still offers living water.
outline: A thirst that well water cannot satisfy (7–15)
A town brought to the Savior (27–42)
preaching.watch_for: Watch the woman’s names for Jesus grow: a Jew (4:9), Sir (4:11), a prophet (4:19), possibly the Christ (4:29), and finally, from her town, the Savior of the world (4:42).
